# 1 Clement Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 20

**[TRANSLATOR'S NOTE: Chapter 20 is the crown jewel of 1 Clement — a majestic prose hymn to the ordered cosmos. Every element of creation is shown to be at peace, obeying God's commands without dissent. This is the most beautiful passage in the letter, drawing on Stoic philosophy to paint a portrait of the universe as God's perfectly ordered household. The implied message to Corinth: you are the one discordant note in an otherwise harmonious creation.]**

**20:1** The heavens move under his oversight and submit to him in peace. Day and night complete the courses he set for them and never get in each other's way.

**20:2** The sun, the moon, and the great dance of stars circle in harmony along the orbits he assigned them, never straying from his command.

**20:3** The earth brings forth its fruit season by season in obedience to his will, providing food without complaint for human beings, for animals, and for every creature on its face — never disputing his decrees.

**20:4** The fathomless depths of the abyss and the uncharted regions beneath the earth are held in check by the same commands.

**20:5** The vast basin of the ocean, shaped by his craftsmanship and gathered into its appointed bounds, does not overflow its barriers but does exactly what he commanded:

**20:6** "You shall come no further," he said, "and your waves shall break here." [Job 38:11]

**20:7** The impassable ocean and everything beyond it are governed by the same Master's decrees.

**20:8** Spring, summer, autumn, and winter follow each other in peaceful order.

**20:9** The winds blow their seasonal circuits without interruption. The ever-flowing springs — made for our refreshment and health — never stop offering their life-giving water for human survival.

**20:10** Even the tiniest living creatures gather and live together in peace and harmony.

**20:11** All of this — the great Maker and Master of everything willed it all to exist in peace and harmony. He pours out his goodness on all of creation, but most abundantly on us, who have run to find refuge in his mercy through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**20:12** To him be glory and majesty, world without end. Amen.

---

*PNEUMA renders chapter 20 as the soaring hymn it is — the rhetorical and theological apex of the letter's first half. "The great dance of stars" preserves the Greek cosmological image of *chorous* (choir/dance).*
